purpose: Add source-exact public-domain hymn stanzas and devotional quotations for sermon preparation and presentation slides.

entries.title: His hands securely keep
entries.author: Isaac Watts
entries.text:
His honour is engag'd to save
The meanest of his sheep,
All that his heavenly Father gave
His hands securely keep.
entries.slideText:
All that his heavenly Father gave
His hands securely keep.
entries.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this edition as public domain in the USA; the stanza is verified against the stored text.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed hymn stanza after exposition of Christ's promise to keep His sheep.
entries.reviewNote: This is hymn poetry, not Scripture. Establish assurance from the cited KJV passages and explain the older spelling retained from the source.

entries.title: Everlasting is thy love
entries.author: Isaac Watts
entries.text:
How oft have sin and Satan strove
To rend my soul from thee, my God,
But everlasting is thy love,
And Jesus seals it with his blood.
entries.slideText:
But everlasting is thy love,
And Jesus seals it with his blood.
entries.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this edition as public domain in the USA; the stanza is verified against the stored text.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed poetic transition in a message about God's unchanging promise and the believer's security in Christ.
entries.reviewNote: The stanza is poetic application. Define the covenant and assurance from the governing KJV texts rather than from the hymn alone.

entries.title: Christ and his love fill every thought
entries.author: Isaac Watts
entries.text:
Let sinful sweets be all forgot,
And earth grow less in our esteem;
Christ and his love fill every thought,
And faith and hope be fix'd on him.
entries.slideText:
Christ and his love fill every thought,
And faith and hope be fix'd on him.
entries.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this edition as public domain in the USA; the stanza is verified against the stored text.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed Communion meditation or invitation to set the heart upon Christ.
entries.reviewNote: This is devotional poetry. Keep the ordinance and the believer's hope grounded in the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: The tree of life
entries.author: Isaac Watts
entries.text:
The tree of life that near the throne
In heaven's high garden grows,
Laden with grace, bends gently down
Its ever-smiling boughs.
entries.slideText:
Laden with grace, bends gently down
Its ever-smiling boughs.
entries.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this edition as public domain in the USA; the stanza is verified against the stored text.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed poetic image in a message on the tree of life and the believer's eternal hope.
entries.reviewNote: The garden language is poetic expansion. Read the governing Revelation passages in KJV wording and distinguish text from imagination.

entries.title: To enjoy prayer
entries.author: Austin Phelps
entries.text: To enjoy prayer, we must be used to it.
entries.slideText: To enjoy prayer, we must be used to it.
entries.sourceTitle: The Still Hour; or, Communion with God
entries.sourceLocator: Chapter VII, The Temperament of Prayer, page 36
entries.rightsBasis: The 1860 edition is public domain in the United States; this sentence is verified against the stored OCR and should still be checked against the page scan before publication.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as a concise attributed prompt for teaching consistency and perseverance in private prayer.
entries.reviewNote: Do not treat devotional enjoyment as the measure of faithful prayer. Establish the duty and privilege of prayer from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Prayer is emotive
entries.author: Austin Phelps
entries.text: Especially is it true, that prayer is in its nature emotive.
entries.slideText: Especially is it true, that prayer is in its nature emotive.
entries.sourceTitle: The Still Hour; or, Communion with God
entries.sourceLocator: Chapter VII, The Temperament of Prayer, page 36
entries.rightsBasis: The 1860 edition is public domain in the United States; this excerpt is verified against the stored OCR and should still be checked against the page scan before publication.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed discussion starter about pouring out the heart before God while praying according to Scripture.
entries.reviewNote: Phelps describes one aspect of prayer, not its complete doctrine. Balance feeling with truth, submission, confession, thanksgiving, and petition from the KJV.

entries.title: Love hides even from itself
entries.author: Henry Drummond
entries.text: Love hides even from itself. Love waives even self-satisfaction.
entries.sourceTitle: The Greatest Thing in the World
entries.rightsBasis: The 1890 edition is public domain in the United States; this excerpt is verified against the stored OCR and should still be checked against the page scan before publication.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed reflection on quiet service after reading the governing KJV passages.
entries.reviewNote: This aphorism is not Scripture. Explain biblical charity and humility from the cited texts and avoid making self-forgetfulness a work of merit.

entries.title: Love in little things
entries.author: Henry Drummond
entries.text: And the one secret of politeness is to love. Love cannot behave itself unseemly.
entries.sourceTitle: The Greatest Thing in the World
entries.rightsBasis: The 1890 edition is public domain in the United States; this excerpt is verified against the stored OCR and should still be checked against the page scan before publication.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed prompt about how biblical charity governs ordinary conduct toward others.
entries.reviewNote: Courtesy is an application, not a substitute for the biblical doctrine of charity. Let the cited KJV passages govern the point.
